posts.subtitle: Set up your ESP32 development environment with Visual Studio Code and PlatformIO, from your first project to uploading code and debugging through the Serial Monitor.
posts.description: Learn how to program an ESP32 using VS Code and PlatformIO. Create your first project, configure the board, upload code, and use the Serial Monitor.

posts.title: A Small Change in How We'll Learn ESP32
posts.subtitle: Clarification About our Approach Philosophy
posts.description: SiliconPen provides clarification regarding the appraoch to the \"Guide To ESP32\" series

posts.title: ESP32 Pinout Explained: GPIO, ADC, PWM, SPI and I²C
posts.subtitle: Your practical guide to understanding ESP32 pins, choosing the right GPIOs, and connecting your first sensors, displays, and actuators.
posts.description: Learn ESP32 pinouts, GPIO, ADC, PWM, UART, SPI, and I²C. Understand pin restrictions and choose the right pins for sensors, displays, and embedded projects.

posts.title: ESP32 Explained: What It Is and What You Can Build With It
posts.subtitle: From a tiny microcontroller to wireless devices, robotics, and even arcade games — let's explore the ESP32.
posts.description: Learn ESP32 with me, and make interesting projects! Get in depth concept, free project files and guidance!

posts.title: Loop Conditions & Decisions in Embedded Systems
posts.subtitle: How Arduino Uses Logic to Think, React, and Make Real Decisions
posts.description: Learn how Arduino makes decisions using loops, conditions, and control flow. This chapter explains how embedded systems think, react, and choose actions based on real-world inputs — the foundation of intelligent behavior in electronics.

posts.title: Variables, Functions & Clean Code Structure
posts.subtitle: How to Organize Your Arduino Programs So They Stay Clean, Simple, and Easy to Fix
posts.description: Your Arduino code works—but it’s getting messy. This chapter teaches how to use variables, functions, and clean code structure to organize your programs, avoid repetition, and make changes easily. Perfect for beginners leveling up their coding skills.

posts.title: Serial Monitor: Your First Debug Tool
posts.subtitle: The Window That Lets You See What Your Arduino Is Really Doing
posts.description: Learn how to use the Arduino Serial Monitor to debug your code, view sensor values, and understand what your program is thinking. A beginner-friendly chapter on printing, monitoring, and troubleshooting real-time data.

posts.title: Delays vs Non-Blocking Code millis()
posts.subtitle: Why delay() Freezes Your Arduino — and How millis() Frees It
posts.description: Using delay() works for beginners, but it stops your Arduino from doing multiple tasks. This chapter explains why delay() becomes a bottleneck and how millis() helps you write smooth, non-blocking, multitasking-friendly code.

posts.title: Understanding PWM & LED Fading
posts.subtitle: How Arduino Fakes Analog Output Using High-Speed Digital Switching
posts.description: If Arduino can only output HIGH or LOW, how does it control brightness or motor speed? This chapter explains Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) in simple terms—how it fakes analog output and lets you fade LEDs or control power smoothly.

posts.title: Using Potentiometers & Mapping Values
posts.subtitle: Transforming Raw Analog Values into Useful Ranges for Real-World Control
posts.description: Learn how to use potentiometers with Arduino and convert raw analogRead() values into useful ranges. This chapter explains voltage division, reading 0–1023 values, and mapping them to angles, brightness, speed, or any custom scale.

posts.title: Analog Input: Reading Sensors with analogRead()
posts.subtitle: How Arduino Measures the Real World Through Voltage Levels and Sensors
posts.description: Learn how Arduino reads real-world signals using analogRead(). This chapter explains analog inputs, voltage levels, and how sensors provide continuous values instead of simple HIGH/LOW signals. Perfect for beginners exploring sensors and data.

posts.title: Potentiometer
posts.subtitle: The Variable Resistor That Lets You Control Electronics Smoothly
posts.description: A beginner-friendly look at potentiometers—what they are, how they work, and why they let humans control circuits smoothly instead of just ON/OFF. Clear, practical, and perfect for real-world electronics learning.

posts.title: Debouncing: Why Buttons Misbehave
posts.subtitle: Understanding Switch Bounce and How Arduino Handles Noisy Button Presses
posts.description: Learn why a simple button press can cause multiple signals in Arduino. This chapter explains the physics behind switch bounce, how it affects digital inputs, and the practical debouncing techniques used in real electronics.

posts.title: From Confusion to Curiosity — One Year of SiliconPen
posts.subtitle: Learning didn’t start with answers — it started with taking the steps!
posts.description: SiliconPen began with confusion—not clarity. This New Year reflection looks back at one year of questioning, unlearning, and rebuilding understanding in electronics, moving from memorized formulas to real curiosity and intuition.

posts.title: Using Digital Inputs In Arduino
posts.subtitle: How Arduino Listens to the World Through Buttons, Switches, and Digital Input Signals
posts.description: Learn how digital inputs work in Arduino using buttons and switches. Understand how the board listens to external signals, reads HIGH/LOW states, and reacts to real-world interactions. Perfect for beginners building interactive projects.

posts.title: Switches
posts.subtitle: A Hands-On Look at How Switches Behave in Real Circuits
posts.description: Understand switches the right way—by seeing how they feel, behave, and connect in real circuits. No theory overload. Just a clear, practical explanation of what a switch actually is and how it controls current in your projects.

posts.description: Before building projects or writing code, you need to understand the core electronic components you’ll work with. This post introduces the fundamental parts—what they do, how they behave, and how they fail—in a simple, practical way.

posts.title: Overview: Real Circuits

posts.description: Electronics is more than equations and more than plug-and-play tutorials. This overview of the Real Circuits series explains the gap between theory and practical circuits, showing how components behave in real life and why that matters.

posts.title: Understanding Digital Output
posts.subtitle: HIGHs and LOWs of the Arduino World!
posts.description: Learn what digital output truly means in electronics. Go beyond code and understand how Arduino pins use HIGH and LOW signals to control real components like LEDs, sensors, and modules. Perfect for beginners exploring embedded systems.
